summary: COMPLETENESS is clean: all 89 confirmed old findings (of 92; 3 old refuted = TMD-DOC-5, TST-cover-8, XC-numbox-MEM-2 correctly excluded) are classified exactly once across the mapper files. No missing IDs and no true double-classification -- BLD-DES-1 and BLD-DES-3 each appear as 'covered' in their unit mapper AND 'missed' in audit-adoptions.json, but the supersede rule counts each once (their covering current finding was refuted, so the adoption supersedes). COVERED-CLAIM AUDIT: all 5 high-severity old findings are genuinely covered (same root cause + >=1 confirmed covering finding), with BLD-DES-1 resolved via confirmed REC-BLD-DES-1; a 12-finding medium/low spot-check spread across DCK-sig, DCK-wrap, DCK-wrap-SEC, TST-cover, TST-MEM, EX-common, EX-os, EX-irr, TMD-DOC, UTL-SEC, XC-numbox and DOC-acc all check out as genuine root-cause matches (incl. file-relocations DCK-wrap-SEC-1->UTL-SEC-1 and UTL-SEC-2->UTL-SEC-1, and the many-to-many EX-os remap). ADOPTIONS: 14 REC-* confirmed, 3 refuted (REC-DBU-MEM-1, REC-DCK-sig-DES-1, REC-PBR-DES-4); every recommended REC has a verdict file (unverifiedRecIds empty). The 3 refuted adoptions create no real gaps: REC-DCK-sig-DES-1 and REC-PBR-DES-4 were refuted as duplicates whose substance is already carried by confirmed current DCK-sig-DES-1 and PBR-DES-1/PBR-DES-2 respectively (mapper attribution errors), and REC-DBU-MEM-1 was refuted because the current review had already consciously assessed that ctypes.data lifetime hazard as a caller-responsibility non-defect (documented in findings/DBU-MEM.json notes). CONCLUSION: the current review plus the 14 CONFIRMED REC-* adoptions IS effectively a complete superset of everything still-valid from the old review -- every still-valid old finding's substance is present in some confirmed current finding or confirmed adoption. The only blemishes are attribution/bookkeeping (PBR-COR-1's cover row points at a refuted finding rather than its confirmed twins; two refuted RECs were really already-covered duplicates) plus the single low-severity DBU-MEM-1 ctypes.data hazard that the current review deliberately downgraded to a documented non-issue.
